title: Infra playbook: GPU fleet, IaC modules, CI/CD and runbooks
author: Priya Nandakumar
content:
Overview:

This playbook consolidates operational guidance, IaC standards, CI/CD patterns, and runbooks for the GPU fleet and supporting infra (cloud accounts, networking, and build pipelines). It is intended for infra engineers, SREs, and platform owners who provision, operate, and scale GPU-backed inference clusters across hosted and private deployments.

Scope:
- GPU fleet capacity planning and scaling policy
- Terraform / IaC module conventions and example usage
- CI/CD pipelines for infra modules and node images
- Operational runbooks for common incidents and day-2 ops
- Cross-team ownership, SLAs, and escalation paths

Key contacts and ownership:
- Infra team owner: Priya Nandakumar (infra-gpu)
- SRE owner: Samir Patel (eng-sre)
- Platform CI owner: Jenna Morales (eng-platform)
- Oncall rotation: infra-oncall (pager duty)

Architecture summary:
- Control plane: managed control services in our cloud account per region (accounts: prod-us-west, prod-eu, staging-us)
- GPU compute: autoscaling GPU node pool (k8s nodepools or managed instance groups) placed in dedicated GPU subnets with private routing
- Images: golden GPU node image containing NVidia drivers, container runtime, and redwood-inference-agent
- IaC: Terraform modules under modules/compute/gpu, modules/networking, modules/cloud-accounts
- CI/CD: Pipelines in GitHub Actions for module lint/test and in Buildkite for image builds and canary deploys

SLOs and operational thresholds:
- API latency SLO (p99): <= 250ms for short text workloads; monitor token-latency per model route
- Node availability SLO: 99.9% per region for dedicated pools
- Capacity buffer policy: maintain a 20% spare capacity buffer above steady-state RPS forecast for production regions
- Scaling decisions: trigger scale-up when queue length > 30s average or GPU utilization > 75% for 5m

Capacity planning procedure (high level):
1) Forecast expected token throughput and peaks from product roadmap and billing signals.
2) Convert throughput to GPU-hours using benchmark profiles from gpu-perf-benchmarks repository.
3) Apply safety multipliers (1.2 steady buffer, 1.5 for launch window).
4) Open capacity request and link to cloud quota requests at least 14 days before expected need.

Scaling & autoscaling policy (k8s/GKE example):
- HorizontalPodAutoscaler for inference-service scaled by request latency and queue depth metrics
- Cluster autoscaler with GPU-aware provisioning and custom node-pool min/max settings
- Reserve spot/burst pool for 15% of peak traffic with automated fallback to on-demand if capacity shortage detected

Terraform / IaC module conventions:
- Module naming: modules/<concern>/<resource> (example: modules/compute/gpu-nodepool)
- Each module must expose: inputs.tf (inputs with descriptions), outputs.tf (key outputs), variables documented in README.md
- Modules must be idempotent and support resource tagging: team, env, cost-center, region

Example module usage (snippet):
- module "gpu_nodepool" {
    source = 'git::ssh://git.company.com/infra/modules//compute/gpu-nodepool?ref=v1.4.0'
    name = 'inference-gpu-01'
    region = 'us-west1'
    min_size = 3
    max_size = 60
    gpu_type = 'nvidia-a100'
    node_image = 'projects/redwood/gpu-node-image:v2026-02-10'
  }

(Replace single quotes in snippet above with double quotes inside real terraform files)

Module testing and CI conventions:
- Pull requests must include: terraform fmt, tflint, and plan output in comments for change review
- Use terratest (go) or kitchen-terraform for integration tests in a sandbox account
- Merge gating: at least one approver from infra-team and CI green

CI/CD pipelines and image build:
- Image build pipeline (Buildkite): 1) checkout 2) build gpu node image 3) run integration smoke tests 4) publish to private registry 5) sign image
- Infra module pipeline (GitHub Actions): lint -> unit tests -> terraform plan -> post plan as comment -> manual apply via CI service account for prod
- Canary deployment pattern: deploy to staging, run synthetic traffic, monitor latency and error rate for 30m, then promote

Network and cloud account guidance:
- Account model: one shared infra account per environment and one tenant account per customer in private deployments
- VPC design: separate GPU subnets, control-plane subnets, and management subnets; enforce egress rules to limit cross-account traffic
- Peering and transit: use shared transit/edge routers for cross-region model artifacts distribution

Runbooks (operational procedures):
- Incident: GPU node failure
  1) Pager triggers to infra-oncall.
  2) Run diagnostics: check node status kubectl get nodes -o wide and check dmesg, nvidia-smi.
  3) If node unrecoverable, cordon and drain: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data.
  4) Verify cluster autoscaler replaced node pool capacity within 5-10m; if not, escalate to cloud-ops to expand quota.
  5) Post-incident: capture node logs, and create postmortem if impact > 5% traffic or > 15m degradation.

- Incident: Sudden capacity shortage / long request queues
  1) Verify metrics: GPU utilization, queue depth, pending pods.
  2) If autoscaler stuck, check provider quotas and cluster autoscaler logs.
  3) Trigger emergency scale-up: temporarily increase nodepool max_size and manually start instances via cloud console if needed.
  4) Failover: route traffic to fallback region/model variant per smart-routing policy.
  5) Communicate via status page and product-alerts channel.

Release and rollback checklist for infra changes:
- Pre-merge: terraform fmt, tflint, unit tests, plan posted
- Pre-apply in staging: run end-to-end tests, synthetic traffic for 1 hour
- Apply to prod: small change window, monitor for 30m, fast rollback plan in place
- Rollback steps: revert terraform change, apply, and if node-image change revert to previous signed image and redeploy nodepool

Common commands and diagnostics:
- Terraform plan for module: terraform init && terraform plan -var-file=env/us-west.tfvars
- Check node image version: gcloud compute images list --filter='name~gpu-node-image'
- View autoscaler events: kubectl describe deployment inference-service | grep -i autoscaler -A 5

Security and compliance notes:
- All modules must accept kms_key_id and enable CMEK for storage where customer data stored
- Audit logs: enable resource-level audit logging for node lifecycle and image builds
- Access: limit who can approve prod apply to infra-maintainers group

Oncall runbook summary and escalation:
- Severity 1: complete region outage impacting > 50% traffic -> escalate to Head of Infra and Eng-SRE within 15 minutes
- Severity 2: degraded latency > 30m impacting critical customers -> paged to infra-oncall and platform lead
- Pager duty playbook link: /confluence/eng-infra/oncall-and-incident-response/pagerduty-playbook

Operational metrics to monitor continuously:
- GPU utilization per pool (5m and 1h)
- Pending pod queue depth and request latency (p50/p95/p99)
- Node launch time and replacement latency
- Image build failure rate

FAQ and troubleshooting tips:
- Why did the cluster autoscaler not replace nodes? Common causes: insufficient cloud quota, taints preventing scheduling, or IAM permission errors on CI service account.
- How to backfill capacity quickly? Use burst-on-demand nodepools with on-demand instances and increase max_size for short windows.
